subject: Vocabulary
topic: Word Analogy — Advanced Relationships and Vocabulary (W12 B1)

questions.explanation: A is correct. Relationship: ANTONYM pairs. MENDACIOUS (habitually lying) is the opposite of TRUTHFUL (honest). PARSIMONIOUS (excessively unwilling to spend; miserly) is the opposite of GENEROUS (willing to give freely). Trap: FRUGAL = careful with money (a milder form of parsimony, actually a near-synonym, not antonym); MISERLY = same as parsimonious (synonym, not antonym). The relationship is ANTONYM so we need the opposite.

A is correct. Relationship: TOOL : USER. A stethoscope is the diagnostic tool used by a doctor. A sextant is a navigational instrument used by a navigator to measure angles between celestial objects and determine position at sea. Trap: astronomer = uses a telescope; surveyor = uses a theodolite; soldier = uses weapons/equipment. A sextant is specifically a maritime/aerial navigation tool.

B is correct. Relationship: STUDY OF : SUBJECT. Ornithology is the scientific study of birds. Entomology is the scientific study of insects (Greek entomos = cut in sections/notched, referring to insects' segmented bodies). Trap: plants = botany; reptiles = herpetology; fossils = palaeontology. Key: entomo = insect (entomologist studies insects).

B is correct. Relationship: ANTONYM pairs. LOQUACIOUS (talkative) is opposite to TACITURN (reserved, saying little). FRUGAL (careful with money, economical) is opposite to EXTRAVAGANT (spending excessively). Trap: THRIFTY = near-synonym of frugal (not antonym); MISERLY = also near-synonym (extreme frugality); CAREFUL = partial synonym of frugal. The antonym of frugal is extravagant/wasteful/spendthrift.

C is correct. Relationship: PRIMARY TOOL MATERIAL : USER. Ink is the primary medium used by a calligrapher (one who practises decorative handwriting). A chisel is the primary tool used by a sculptor (one who carves/shapes stone, wood or metal). Trap: carpenter = uses a saw, hammer, nails (chisel is used by both carpenters and sculptors, but a sculptor's PRIMARY tool is the chisel for shaping; a painter uses brushes/paint not chisels).

C is correct. Relationship: ANTONYM pairs. FORTITUDE (courage in facing adversity) is opposite to COWARDICE (lack of courage). CANDOUR (frankness, honesty, openness) is opposite to DECEIT (dishonesty, concealment, trickery). Trap: SINCERITY and HONESTY are near-synonyms of candour (not antonyms); BOLDNESS = near-synonym of fortitude (not relevant to candour). The pattern is consistently antonyms.

B is correct. Relationship: YOUNG ONE : SPECIES. A fledgling is a young bird that has recently grown its feathers (generic young bird). A cygnet is specifically the young of a swan. Trap: duck's young = duckling; eagle's young = eaglet; goose's young = gosling. The classic set SSC loves: cygnet (swan), foal (horse), calf (cow/elephant), lamb (sheep), kitten (cat), puppy (dog), leveret (hare), fawn (deer).

C is correct. Relationship: ANTONYM pairs. LACONIC (using very few words; brief) is opposite to VERBOSE (using too many words; long-winded). ERUDITE (having or showing great learning) is opposite to IGNORANT (lacking knowledge or education). Trap: LEARNED, SCHOLARLY, STUDIOUS = all near-synonyms of ERUDITE (not antonyms). The pattern demands antonyms throughout.

C is correct. Relationship: ANTONYM pairs. EPHEMERAL (lasting for only a short time; short-lived) is opposite to ENDURING (lasting a long time; permanent). ARCHAIC (very old or old-fashioned; belonging to an earlier period) is opposite to CONTEMPORARY (belonging to or occurring in the present time; modern). Trap: ANCIENT, OUTDATED, OBSOLETE = all near-synonyms of archaic (not antonyms). CONTEMPORARY = modern/current = true antonym of archaic.

A is correct. Relationship: EXPERT : FIELD OF STUDY. A philologist studies the historical development and structure of language. A palaeontologist studies fossils — the preserved remains of prehistoric organisms — to understand ancient life (Greek palaios = ancient + ontos = being + -logia = study). Trap: rocks = geologist; ancient art = archaeologist or art historian; plants = botanist. Palaeontology ≠ geology (though related); fossils are the specific subject.
